tweets: Above the Waghora river, thirty rock-cut sanctuaries hold Buddhism's finest surviving paintings. Artists built the wall in mud-straw plaster finished with lime, then worked tempera pigments in before it fully dried. Cave 17, Vākāṭaka era, 5th century CE.
